description: Agent Capability Registry: URI namespace for agent capabilities (ADR-041), unifying ChallengeType and CapabilityEntry under structured URIs. Three authorities: scp:capability:* (protocol-defined, reserved), did:*:capability:* (DID-scoped custom), scp:system:* (protocol feature flags). 28 challenge capabilities + 5 system capabilities. SDK validation rejects unknown protocol-scoped URIs. Context admission requirements reference capability URIs with verification levels.

stories.title: Implement CapabilityUri type with three-authority URI parser
stories.description: Implement the CapabilityUri validated type that parses and validates agent capability URIs per ADR-041 and §7.3.4.1. Three URI authorities: (1) scp:capability:{kebab-case}/v{N} for protocol-defined challenge capabilities, (2) did:{method}:{id}:capability:{kebab-case}/v{N} for DID-scoped custom capabilities, (3) scp:system:{kebab-case} for protocol feature flags. The parser enforces: kebab-case naming (lowercase ASCII + hyphens), positive integer version numbers, no deeper nesting. CapabilityUri implements Display (round-trips to the canonical URI string), FromStr, Serialize/Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Clone, Debug. Error variants: MalformedUri, InvalidKebabCase, InvalidVersion, UnknownAuthority.
acceptanceCriteria: CapabilityUri enum has three variants: Protocol { name: String, version: u32 }, DidScoped { did: String, name: String, version: u32 }, System { name: String }

FromStr parses 'did:dht:z6Mk123:capability:domain-expertise/v2' into DidScoped { did: "did:dht:z6Mk123", name: "domain-expertise", version: 2 }
FromStr parses 'scp:system:relay-operation' into System { name: "relay-operation" }
FromStr rejects 'scp:capability:UPPERCASE/v1' with InvalidKebabCase error
FromStr rejects 'scp:capability:name/v0' with InvalidVersion error (version must be >= 1)
FromStr rejects 'scp:capability:name' with MalformedUri error (missing version for capability URIs)
FromStr rejects 'scp:unknown:name' with UnknownAuthority error
FromStr rejects 'scp:capability:name/v1/extra' with MalformedUri error (no deeper nesting)
Display round-trips: parse then display produces the original string for all valid URIs
CapabilityUri derives Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Clone, Debug

Tests verify all error variants are reachable

stories.title: Implement protocol capability registry with 28 challenge + 5 system capabilities
stories.description: Implement the protocol capability registry per ADR-041 and §7.3.4.3. The registry is a compile-time constant map from CapabilityUri to RegistryEntry containing category, description, and optional parameter schema (serde_json::Value). The registry contains 28 challenge capabilities across 10 categories and 5 system capabilities. Provides lookup_protocol_capability(uri) -> Option<&RegistryEntry> and is_known_protocol_capability(uri) -> bool. The validate_capability_uri(uri) function rejects unknown scp:capability:* URIs while accepting all valid DID-scoped URIs. This is the SDK enforcement point described in §7.3.4.2.

PROTOCOL_REGISTRY contains exactly 27 entries with CapabilityUri::Protocol variants
SYSTEM_REGISTRY contains exactly 5 entries with CapabilityUri::System variants

lookup_protocol_capability returns None for 'scp:capability:nonexistent/v1'

is_known_protocol_capability returns false for unknown protocol URIs
validate_capability_uri accepts all 28 protocol capabilities
validate_capability_uri accepts arbitrary DID-scoped capabilities without registry lookup

validate_capability_uri accepts all 5 system capabilities
Parameterized capabilities (latency-compliance, multilingual, mathematical-reasoning, code-generation, code-review) have non-None parameter_schema

Tests verify round-trip: every registry entry's URI parses back to the same CapabilityUri

stories.title: Unify ChallengeType enum with CapabilityUri
stories.description: Replace the existing ChallengeType enum's hardcoded variants and Custom(String) with CapabilityUri-based matching per ADR-041 acceptance criterion 3. The three existing variants map to protocol URIs: PromptInjectionResistance -> scp:capability:prompt-injection-resistance/v1, SchemaValidation -> scp:capability:schema-validation/v1, RateLimitCompliance -> scp:capability:rate-limit-compliance/v1. Custom(String) is replaced by a variant that holds a validated CapabilityUri (must be DID-scoped or a known protocol URI). Existing code that pattern-matches on ChallengeType must be updated. The challenge_type_tag function uses the URI string representation. ChallengeRequest and ChallengeResponse are unchanged except for the ChallengeType field type. Serialization must be backwards-compatible: old PromptInjectionResistance deserializes to the URI form.

stories.title: Expand challenge support for all 28 protocol capabilities
stories.description: After SCP-ACR-003 unifies ChallengeType with CapabilityUri, ensure the challenge-response protocol supports all 28 protocol-defined capabilities. The issue_challenge function must accept any valid CapabilityUri (protocol or DID-scoped). The verify_challenge_response function validates against the registry to confirm the challenge type is a known protocol capability or a valid DID-scoped URI. Parameterized capabilities (latency-compliance, multilingual, mathematical-reasoning, code-generation, code-review) must have their parameter schemas available for challenge parameter validation. This story does NOT implement concrete test vectors for each capability; it ensures the infrastructure supports all 28.

stories.title: Update CapabilityEntry to use CapabilityUri type
stories.description: Update CapabilityEntry in did_capabilities.rs to use Vec<CapabilityUri> instead of Vec<String> for the capabilities field per ADR-041 acceptance criterion 4. The parse_capability_endpoint function must parse each comma-separated capability string as a CapabilityUri. stories.title: Add system capability declarations to DID document service entries
stories.description: Extend the DID document capability advertising to support system capabilities (scp:system:*). System capabilities use the same SCPCapabilities service endpoint format as challenge capabilities but with the scp:system: prefix. The parse_capability_endpoint function already handles this via the CapabilityUri parser (SCP-ACR-005), but this story ensures system capabilities are properly represented, documented, and tested. System capabilities describe node roles (relay-operation, bridge-operation, etc.) and are not subject to challenge-response verification. Contexts and peers can discover system capabilities via DID resolution.

stories.title: Implement context admission capability requirements with verification levels
stories.description: Implement the context admission capability requirement system per ADR-041 acceptance criterion 6 and §7.3.4.4. Add a CapabilityRequirement struct containing a CapabilityUri and a VerificationLevel (SelfAttested or ChallengeVerified). Add an optional required_capabilities: Vec<CapabilityRequirement> field to ContextParams (or the relevant admission configuration type). Implement check_capability_requirements(requirements, agent_capabilities, challenge_verifications) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> that validates a joining agent meets all requirements. SelfAttested requires the capability URI in the agent's CapabilityEntry. ChallengeVerified requires a valid ChallengeVerification record for that capability URI. This story does NOT wire the check into the join flow (that depends on the ContextManager integration); it implements the data types and check function.

stories.title: Expose context capability-admission requirements and check_capability_requirements through the FFI bridges and all four SDKs
stories.description: Wire the spec-mandated admission primitive check_capability_requirements (§7.3.4.4, implemented by SCP-ACR-007 but left unwired) through the FFI bridges and all four SDKs, mirroring the fully-wired participation sibling verify_participation_requirements (SCP-BA-004, §7.3.2.1). Unlike participation, this op authenticates caller-supplied ChallengeVerification records and therefore needs a DID resolver and a fail-closed clock: expose it as a per-bridge-instance method using the bridge's existing unified DID resolver (IdentityDidPublicKeyResolver) and SystemClock. The bridge envelope mirrors the sibling: JSON strings in (requirements_json, agent_capabilities_json, challenge_verifications_json, context_id, subject_did), void-plus-throw out, validate_did(subject_did) at each boundary; map AdmissionError::{MissingCapability, VerificationRequired} to the bridge's admission-failure error and AdmissionError::EmptySubjectDid plus JSON parse failures to validation errors with distinct codes. Also close the latent ADR-041 AC6 / SCP-ACR-007 gap: add the missing capability_requirements: Vec<CapabilityRequirement> field to ContextParams, mirroring participation_requirements (default empty vec in every constructor/builder/test site, serde roundtrip test). No WASM bridge (removed per ADR-055). SelfAttested/ChallengeVerified semantics and subject/context binding live in the core primitive (SCP-ACR-007) and are not re-implemented here.
